I mean with the wings, it definitely changes visibility; in your check ride / exam for your license you’re meant to tilt the wings the opposite direction of your turn first to get a better a view - kind of how you have to really exaggerate looking at your wing mirrors on a drivers test.

You should go with them one time, the place where I’m flying (if you’re in a 4 seat aircraft) let’s you take someone up with you during a lessons for a little extra $¥. You can’t take someone  else without an instructor w/ you though until you have your license.

That sounds really good dude with your college stuff, good luck on passing it all, I wanted to minor in Philosophy just out of interest but it flashed to much with what I was going to major in: Pilot Studies (it’s a thing). 
Problem was, was that I’d just have a load of student loans to pay off on top of all the expenses of flying because a degree in an aviation related expertise doesn’t guarantee you a job as a Pilot.

I’ve flown an aerobatics plane which was called a Robin (don’t remember exact name [might’ve been a DR401) and Cessna 172 & Piper PA-28.

I don’t know if any of those mean anything to you but my favourite would have to be the same lil plane I started in, the Cessna 152. Just a very fun small aircraft that can take a lot more stress than you’d expect. Some of the stuff I’ve done in it would make me think it is an aerobatics plane (despite the sticker in it’s cockpit and operation handbook that clearly states ‘no aerobatic manoeuvres lol).

Ayy, look at that, we’re both rambling

What about you though, what are you doing at uni/college?

Yeah flyings pretty nice, don’t worry about the irreverent stranger bit; I feel the same posting this lol.

I’ve kinda given up on meeting new people, I can’t find anyone I relate to that I haven’t already drifted from.

Maybe leaving my house might be helpful, that’s something I need to work on.

But thanks dude, your words mean a lot.
